declarations.docstring: The linear map that regards an algebra-linear map between scalar-tower modules as a linear map over the base ring.
The evaluation map from the direct sum of hom-space tensor products associated with a family of modules into the target module.
The linear equivalence from the direct sum of multiplicity-space tensor products to a finite-dimensional semisimple module whose simple constituents are exhausted by a pairwise inequivalent family.
The isotypic evaluation map is injective for a pairwise inequivalent finite family of finite-dimensional simple modules over an algebraically closed field.
The isotypic evaluation map sends a pure tensor included from one direct-sum component to evaluation of its homomorphism on its vector.
The isotypic evaluation map is surjective when every simple submodule of the semisimple target is equivalent to a member of the indexing family.
The linear evaluation map from the tensor product of algebra-linear maps with their source module into the target module.
For a finite-dimensional simple module over an algebraically closed field, evaluation is a linear equivalence from its algebra-endomorphism space tensored with the module to the module.
The endomorphism-tensor equivalence sends a pure tensor to evaluation of the endomorphism on the vector.
Evaluation from the hom-space tensor product of a finite-dimensional simple module into a finite-dimensional target is injective over an algebraically closed field.
The value of the hom-tensor evaluation map belongs to the isotypic component determined by its simple source module.
The hom-tensor evaluation map sends a pure tensor to application of the homomorphism to the vector.
The isotypic components associated with a pairwise inequivalent family of simple modules in a semisimple module form an independent supremum.
Distinct members of a pairwise inequivalent family have distinct isotypic components whenever the first component is nonzero.
Every linear map between two simple modules is zero when no module-linear equivalence between them exists.
A nonzero isotypic component belongs to the set of isotypic components of the ambient module.
Every simple submodule represented by the indexing family is contained in the range of the isotypic evaluation map.
